cleanIntro: Rossi publishes no takedown for the Gallery. What the book gives you is a safe way to empty the magazine tube and chamber, a check with the action open before cleaning, and a clean done through the open action and down the bore from the muzzle — so that is what this guide walks, and nothing is invented past it.

steps.title: Manual safety on — red band hidden
steps.action: Push the manual safety button at the rear of the receiver across until the red band can no longer be seen. Red band hidden is safe; red band showing means the rifle is ready to fire.
steps.prose: The Gallery carries two separate safety arrangements: the cross-button manual safety and a three-position hammer (down, half-cock, full cock). The button is the one to use while you unload, and the red band is the only test that matters — look at it rather than trusting which way you think you pushed. Keep your finger off the trigger while you set it; Rossi tells you not to touch the trigger while the safety button is being engaged.
steps.caution: The cleaning page of the same book prints the opposite direction for engaging the safety. Go by the red band: hidden is safe, whatever the text on that page says.
steps.quote: When finished shooting, immediately set the manual safety to the safe position by pushing the safety button from left to right.
steps.cite:
OWNER’S MANUAL
Rossi® Gallery — Rev. 00 — To Fire, p.17

steps.title: Open the action — action release first if the hammer is cocked
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, press the action release control on the trigger guard, then pull the forend back to open the action. If the hammer is cocked the forend will not come back until you press the action release.
steps.prose: A cocked Gallery locks its forend closed, which is what stops the action unlocking when you fire. The action release control on the trigger guard is the only way to open it in that state, and Rossi notes that pressing it opens the chamber even when cocked — so a round in the chamber comes out as the forend comes back. Expect that, and have somewhere safe for it to land.
steps.quote: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, press the action release control and then pull the forend back to open the action.
steps.cite:
OWNER’S MANUAL
Rossi® Gallery — Rev. 00 — Loading Your Firearm, p.14

steps.title: Pump it empty — safety on, finger off the trigger
steps.action: With the safety on (red band hidden), pull the forend back to open the action and throw the cartridge out, push it forward, and repeat — without pulling the trigger. Keep going until a full stroke of the forend brings nothing out.
steps.prose: Each stroke lifts the next round out of the tube and ejects the one in the chamber, so the rifle always has one more in it than you have seen come out. Do not count to a capacity you remember; the stop is a stroke that produces nothing. Rossi prints WITHOUT PULLING THE TRIGGER in capitals on this page because the trigger sits right where your hand wraps as you work the forend.
steps.quote: If you want to unload your firearm without shooting, set the manual safety on, (red band is not visible) pull the forend back to open the action
steps.cite:
OWNER’S MANUAL
Rossi® Gallery — Rev. 00 — Unloading Your Firearm, p.18
steps.warn: Always make sure the breech bolt will open in a safe direction and that the unfired cartridges will fall on a safe place. Cartridges ejecting from the chamber can cause injury.

steps.title: Or empty the tube by pulling the inner magazine tube
steps.action: The alternative is to twist the inner magazine tube to release it from the magazine button, pull it out, and tip the live cartridges out of the outer tube. Then still open the action and look: emptying the tube does nothing about a round already in the chamber.
steps.prose: The Gallery feeds from a tube under the barrel with a removable inner tube carrying the spring and the green follower, the same tube you pull to load it. Pulling it empties the magazine but not the chamber, so this route always finishes with the action open and the chamber inspected. Keep the muzzle pointed safely while the tube is out — the cartridges have to slide out of the outer tube toward the loading port.
steps.quote: Or you can twist the inner magazine tube by disengaging the magazine button, pull the tube out, and remove all the live cartridges from the magazine.
steps.cite:
OWNER’S MANUAL
Rossi® Gallery — Rev. 00 — Unloading Your Firearm, p.18

steps.title: Action open, chamber and bore checked — this is the working state
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, manual safety on, forend pulled back so the action stands open. Look into the chamber through the ejection port and down the barrel and bore, and confirm all of it is clear before a rod or a cloth goes near the rifle.
steps.prose: The open action is all the access a Gallery gives you, and it is enough for the clean Rossi publishes: you can see the chamber, the bolt face and the breech, and reach the bore from the muzzle. Look for light through the bore — Rossi's rule is that no light means something is stuck in the barrel, and that rifle is not fired again until a gunsmith has cleared it.
steps.quote: the forend back (see page 6 and 15), visually inspect the chamber, barrel and bore to ensure the firearm is clear and safe to perform cleaning.
steps.cite:
OWNER’S MANUAL
Rossi® Gallery — Rev. 00 — Care and Maintenance, p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete — the Gallery does not come apart here
steps.action: That is as far as this rifle goes. Rossi publishes no takedown for the Gallery — no barrel removal, no bolt removal, no trigger group — and it captions its own parts drawing as an informative guide, not a guide to assembly. Clean it as it stands, with the action open.
steps.prose: The exploded drawing at the back of the book lists some seventy parts, including twin extractors, a locking bolt and a carrier, and it tempts people into a teardown it was never drawn to support. Rossi recommends returning the rifle to Braztech when it needs service and warns that improper fitting or adjustment of parts can cause a dangerous malfunction. If it needs more than a clean and a light oil, it goes to a gunsmith.
steps.quote: This is intended as an informative guide and not a specific model or guide to assembly.
steps.cite:
OWNER’S MANUAL
Rossi® Gallery — Rev. 00 — Drawing and Parts List, p.20

deepAbsentReason: Rossi's Gallery book stops at a clean through the open action: a cleaning rod with a lightly oiled patch run from the muzzle toward the breech, a swab for the chamber, bolt face and breech, and a lightly oiled cloth over the rifle (Care and Maintenance and Cleaning Instructions, p.19). The only disassembly it prints is the front sight, for sight adjustment (pp.16–17). Its parts drawing is captioned as an informative guide and not a guide to assembly (p.20), and it recommends returning the rifle to Braztech for service (p.22). There is no deeper procedure in the book to walk.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean the rifle after every use — Rossi's instruction is to always clean it after use

With the action open, run a cleaning rod with a lightly oiled patch from the muzzle end down toward the breech, cleaning the chamber as it goes — the Gallery does not come apart, so the muzzle is the way in
Swab all debris out of the chamber and off the face of the bolt and the breech — Rossi calls a clean chamber and bolt face important
Leave the bore clean and free of debris, then look through it for light: no light means something is lodged in the barrel
Never try to shoot out or blow out an obstruction with another cartridge or a blank — take the rifle to a qualified gunsmith or Rossi's service department

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, FOREND & TUBE
tasks: Rub the outside of the rifle with a lightly oiled cloth, leaving a light film of good quality gun oil against corrosion
Brush dust out of every crevice with a small clean plastic brush — the ejection port and the loading port in the outer magazine tube are where it collects
Remove excess oil; oil left standing in the action collects the dust you have just brushed out

cleaning.name: CHECKS WHILE IT IS OPEN
tasks: Rossi asks for a qualified gunsmith's check every year even when the rifle seems to work well, because wear and corrosion inside may not show from outside
If the rifle has been dropped or struck, it goes to a qualified armorer or gunsmith for a complete function check before it is used again
⚠ If you notice any mechanical malfunction, stop using the rifle, unload it and take it to a qualified gunsmith

reassembly: Nothing was taken apart. If you pulled the inner magazine tube to unload, push it back down into position and lock it with the magazine button — slowly, because Rossi warns it is under spring tension, and with the muzzle and the tube pointed in a safe direction.
Close the action by pushing the forend fully forward. Working the forend cocks the hammer, so check the manual safety is on (red band hidden) the moment the action closes.

If you want the hammer at the safety (half-cocked) position for storage, do it only with the chamber confirmed empty and exactly as the book teaches: muzzle safe, hold the hammer back firmly with your thumb, press the trigger just enough to release it, take your finger off the trigger and ease the hammer down until it locks in the safety position.
Store the rifle unloaded and locked with the ammunition kept somewhere else, and never lock it with a round in the chamber.
fncheck: Chamber confirmed empty and muzzle safe: the forend should run fully back and forward without binding, opening and closing the action; with the hammer cocked the forend should stay locked until you press the action release control on the trigger guard; the manual safety button should push across so the red band disappears and back so it shows again; and with the hammer set in the safety (half-cocked) position, a press of the trigger should not let the hammer fall. Do all of this with an empty rifle and your thumb controlling the hammer. If anything is vague, notchy or will not repeat, the rifle goes to a qualified gunsmith rather than back in the safe.
